MACT AT BIDAR, SITTING INTINERARY COURT AT AURAD-B IN MVC No. 154/2011 AND ENHANCE THE COMPENSATION AMOUNT AS CLAIMED BY THE APPELLANT, AND FIX THE LIABILITY ON THE 2ND RESPONDENT.

THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

The claimant is in appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT at Bidar sitting Itinerary Court at Aurad-B (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC No.154/2011, vide judgment and award dated 10.02.2014.

entities.text: Bidar sitting Itinerary Court at Aurad-B
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The claimant claimed that he was a coolie in a tractor bearing registration No.KA-38/T-1966.
He claimed that on 28.12.2010, when he was working in the tractor, he suffered injuries, when the driver of the tractor drove it in a rash and negligent manner and caused an accident.
The claimant claimed that he had suffered bleeding injuries on his right leg and he was shifted to Udaygiri Multi Specialty Hospital, Udgir, where he underwent a surgery for fixing the fractures.
He claimed that he was earning a sum of Rs.10,000/- per month and he suffered NC: 2023:KHC-K:1238 disability due to the accident.
He therefore filed a claim petition claming compensation from the owner and insurer of the tractor.
3. The owner of the tractor claimed that the tractor was loaded with building stones and therefore, it was not possible for the driver to drive it in a rash and negligent manner.
He also denied that the claimant was employed as a coolie.
He contended that the claimant was intoxicated and tried to climb on to the tractor but fell down and suffered injuries.

4. The insurer on the other hand also denied the accident but claimed that the driver of the tractor did not possess a licence and therefore, the owner of the tractor had violated the conditions of the policy of insurance.
5. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant was examined as PW.1 and he marked Exs.P1 to P29.

A representative of the insurer was examined as RW.1 and he marked Exs.R1 to R3.

2 6.
Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the claimant proved that he suffered injuries in the accident caused by rash and negligent driving by the driver of the tractor.
It also held that the claimant had suffered injuries namely, fracture of right femur and had undergone treatment at Udaygiri Multi Specialty Hospital, Udgir for 14 days.

However, since the claimant did not examine any medical professional to assess the disability, the Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.72,600/- being the medical expenses payable by the owner of the tractor along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization since it was claimed that the tractor was used to transport building stones on rental basis while the insurance policy was a farmers package policy.
Being aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the claimant is in appeal.

7. Learned counsel for the appellant/claimant contended that the evidence on record clearly indicated NC: 2023:KHC-K:1238 that the claimant had suffered fracture of right femur and he had undergone treatment for a period of 14 days.
He submitted that the documents placed on record clearly indicated that the claimant had suffered some amount of disability.
He contends that the Tribunal must have considered some amount of disability based on its experience while dealing with similar matters.

He contended that the Tribunal had assessed the notional income of the claimant at a sum of Rs.3,000/- per month while this Court has consistently considered the notional income at a sum of Rs.5,500/- per month.
He submitted that the compensation awarded under the conventional heads also warrants enhancement.

8. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/insurer contended that the insurer was not liable to pay the compensation as the tractor was used for commercial purpose namely, transportation of building stones on rental basis while it was only be used for the purposes of agriculture.
He therefore contends that it is NC: 2023:KHC-K:1238 not liable to pay the compensation and the Tribunal had rightly fastened the liability on the owner of the tractor.
9. The owner of the tractor though served, remained absent.
10. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellant/claimant as well as the learned counsel for the respondent/insurer.
11. The accident involving the tractor is not in dispute.
It is also not in dispute that the claimant had suffered injuries in the accident and consequent treatment availed by him is also not in dispute.
The claimant claimed to be a coolie, which too is not contested by the insurer and therefore, fracture of femur would result in some amount of disability.
The Tribunal instead of ignoring the disability suffered, must have assessed the disability based upon its experience while dealing in similar cases.
Therefore, the disability suffered by the claimant deserves to be assessed at 10% to the whole body.
As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the NC: 2023:KHC-K:1238 appellant/claimant, the income of the claimant ought to have been considered at a sum of Rs.5,500/-.
In that view of the matter, the compensation to which the claimant is entitled deserves to be enhanced and the same is re
-determined as follows:

Pain and suffering Rs.20,000/-

removal of implants Total Rs.2,11,100/-
 12.
In so far as the liability to pay the compensation is concerned, the tractor was undoubtedly insured under the farmers package policy and the tractor was not to be used for commercial purposes.
PW.1 in his evidence claimed that the tractor was used to transport NC: 2023:KHC-K:1238 the building stones on rental basis.
The owner however did not turn up to contest his claim.
Therefore, there was a clear violation of the policy conditions by using the tractor for commercial purposes and therefore there was clear breach of the policy conditions.
13. In that view of the matter, the owner of the tractor was liable to pay the compensation.

However,
violation of the policy conditions cannot result in absolutely exonerating the insurer from its liability to indemnify the owner.
Therefore, the insurer of the tractor is liable to pay the compensation as re-determined by this Court along with interest and recover it from the owner.

14. In view of the above, the appeal is allowed in part and the compensation of Rs.72,600/-
determined by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.2,11,100/-.
The enhanced compensation of Rs.1,38,500/- shall be paid by the insurer to the claimants along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.

The enhanced compensation amount along with interest shall be deposited by the insurer before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment and award.
Upon deposit, 50% of the enhanced compensation and interest shall be deposited in the name of the claimant, in any nationalized Bank for a period of 3 years.
